previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted for shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain, found to be due to acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation with volume overload, leading to pulmonary edema and cardiorenal syndrome. She also presented with acute blood loss anemia, likely from recent severe epistaxis, on a background of chronic anemia from end-stage renal disease, requiring three units of packed red blood cells. Her kidney transplant function remained stable on imaging, and worsening creatinine improved with diuresis. A chronic right acetabular fracture was incidentally noted on CT and managed nonoperatively. Hypertension was managed with discontinuation of amlodipine and initiation of labetalol. Seizure prophylaxis with levetiracetam was continued, and medication adherence was reinforced. She improved clinically, with resolution of pulmonary edema on repeat imaging, weight reduction from 86.7 kg to 78.1 kg, and stabilization of hemoglobin at 7.8 g/dL. She was discharged home with service on increased furosemide, labetalol, and a short-term opioid supply, with follow-up arranged in heart failure, nephrology, and orthopedic clinics.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic heart failure exacerbation
Acute blood loss anemia on anemia of chronic disease

TECHNIQUE:  Multidetector CT images of the abdomen and pelvis were acquired
without intravenous contrast. Non-contrast scan has several limitations in
detecting vascular and parenchymal organ abnormalities, including tumor
detection.
Coronal and sagittal reformations were performed and reviewed on PACS.

Oral contrast was administered.

DOSE:  DLP:  698.58 mGy-cm (abdomen and pelvis).

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen and pelvis ___.

FINDINGS: 

LOWER CHEST:  Mild bibasilar atelectasis. There is no evidence of pleural or
pericardial effusion.

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions.  There is no evidence of intrahepatic
or extrahepatic biliary dilatation.  The gallbladder is surgically absent.

PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of
focal lesions or pancreatic ductal dilatation. There is no peripancreatic
stranding.

SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.

ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.

URINARY: The native kidneys are markedly atrophic.  A non-obstructing stone in
the left kidney measures 3 mm.  A left lower quadrant kidney transplant
appears normal, without evidence of hydronephrosis or stones.  There is no
perinephric abnormality.

GASTROINTESTINAL:  There is a small hiatal hernia. Small bowel loops
demonstrate normal caliber and wall thickness throughout. Colon and rectum are
within normal limits. Appendix contains air, has normal caliber without
evidence of fat stranding. There is no evidence of mesenteric lymphadenopathy.

RETROPERITONEUM: There is no evidence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.

VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. There is no calcium burden in
the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable. There is no
evidence of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. There is no free fluid in the
pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Reproductive organs are within normal limits.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES: There is a known right acetabular and right superior
ramus fracture.  There is spinal hardware extending from the L3 vertebral body
into the sacrum and marked degenerative changes including grade 3
anterolisthesis of L4 on L5.

IMPRESSION:


1. No findings to explains the patient's abdominal pain.  Specifically, no
small-bowel obstruction or colitis.
2. Skin thickening and subjacent fat stranding in the left abdominal wall soft
tissues raises concern for cellulitis.
3. 3 mm left non-obstructing kidney stone.

There is normal compressibility, flow and augmentation of the left common

Limited evaluation of the calf veins.  No evidence of deep venous thrombosis

EXAMINATION:  RENAL TRANSPLANT U.S. PORT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with history of deceased donor kidney
transplant in ___ presenting with periumbilical abdominal pain x 1 day.

TECHNIQUE:  Grey scale as well as color and spectral Doppler ultrasound images
of the renal transplant were obtained.

COMPARISON:  Renal transplant ultrasound from ___.

FINDINGS: 

The left iliac fossa transplant renal morphology is normal.  Specifically, the
cortex is of normal thickness and echogenicity, pyramids are normal, there is
no urothelial thickening, and renal sinus fat is normal.  There is mild
pelviectasis, new since prior examination.  There is no perinephric fluid
collection.  The bladder was not seen.

The resistive index of intrarenal arteries ranges from 0.67 to 0.72, within
the normal range.  The main renal artery shows a normal waveform, with prompt
systolic upstroke and continuous antegrade diastolic flow, with peak systolic
velocity of 60.9 cm/sec.. Vascularity is symmetric throughout transplant. The
transplant renal vein is patent and shows normal waveform.

IMPRESSION: 

Mild pelviectasis in the transplanted kidney, new since prior examination. 
Otherwise, unremarkable renal transplant ultrasound.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

Similar appearance to prior with methylmethacrylate spacer at the site of
previous knee arthroplasty.  Intra medullary wire and cement in the distal
femur and proximal tibia partly visualized.  Thick periosteal reaction in the
distal femur appears similar to previous.  The tibial and fibular fractures
seen on prior exam are not included in the field of view.  The intramedullary

EXAMINATION:  TIB/FIB (AP AND LAT) LEFT

INDICATION:  ___ year old woman with complicated history of orthopedic
intervention on Left lower extremity.  // Please include tibia/fibula.
Osteomyelitis of tibia/fibula, draining sinus tract evaluation

TECHNIQUE:  Four views of the left tibia and fibula.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS: 

Again seen are the oblique fractures of the distal diaphysis of the left tibia
and fibula with mild  angulation.  The alignment is unchanged.  Fracture lines
remain visible and there is significant surrounding callus formation.  Of
note, there is a methylmethacrylate spacer at the knee joint. 
Methylmethacrylate extends along the wire in the diaphysis of the tibia. 
Lateral subluxation of the tibia and fibula along with the methylmethacrylate
spacer with respect to the distal femur is again seen.  Multiple dystrophic
calcifications are seen in the soft tissues.

IMPRESSION: 

Interval callus formation of the distal tibia and fibular fractures consistent
with healing.  Unchanged alignment.
